field.label: Tunnel
field.help: Fixed: the name, instance number, device, interface and gateway names never change, so gateway groups and rules that name the tunnel keep working.

field.label: Tunnel References
field.help: Where the rest of this tunnel is configured; Edit changes only the fields below. Gateways: thresholds, monitoring and kill states (each link opens that gateway). Gateway groups: membership and tiers. Firewall rules: opens on the tunnel interface. Outbound NAT: filtered to the tunnel interface, for the rules Edit does not list. Peer: keepalive and allowed IPs. Interface: its settings; an MTU set there overrides the instance MTU.

field.label: Replacement config
field.help: Optional: a new wg-quick file for this tunnel (another server, or new keys): paste it, or use "Load file" (read by your browser; nothing is uploaded). It replaces the instance key pair, the peer's public and preshared keys, the endpoint and the tunnel addresses; the old endpoint's route is deleted, with its kernel route, and one to the new endpoint written via the bound WAN. Leave it empty to keep them. The private key is never shown again.

field.label: Bound WAN
field.help: Moves the tunnel to another WAN: its endpoint route changes gateway and the tunnel restarts, so it handshakes via that WAN. An unbound tunnel is bound with Rebind.

field.label: Monitor IP
field.help: An IPv4 address pinged through the tunnel. Nothing else may use it: no other gateway's monitor or address, no DNS server or forwarder, no endpoint.

field.label: MTU
field.help: The instance MTU, 1280 to 1420. Measure probes from the chosen WAN to the endpoint (the replacement config's, when one is pasted). A change restarts the tunnel; the MSS clamp follows. An MTU set on the interface itself still wins (finding mtu-override).

field.label: IPv6
field.help: Unticking removes the IPv6 gateway (refused while a group or rule uses it), the IPv6 tunnel address, ::/0 from the peer and the IPv6 outbound NAT. Ticking needs a replacement config with an IPv6 Address, since the provider assigns it with the key; the new IPv6 gateway starts forced down and the health mirror releases it.

field.label: Unique addressing
field.help: With a replacement config: give the tunnel fd00::N:1/128 instead of the config's IPv6 address, as Create does. The provider must accept and translate the substituted source address.

field.label: IPv4 NAT sources
field.help: Select an interface or alias to add one outbound NAT rule for it (destination any, translated to the tunnel's address). Deselect it to delete every rule on this interface with that source. Every other rule, and every other field of a kept rule, stays as it is.
